knowledge-base.overview: ASP.NET Core 8.x guardrails, Clean Architecture patterns, Minimal APIs, EF Core, middleware, FluentValidation, and testing. Applies to Web APIs and MVC apps using C# 12 with Nullable reference types enabled. Loaded automatically when agents work on .cs or .csproj files targeting net8.0+.

core-principles.principle: Separate API, Core (domain), Infrastructure, and Contracts layers. Core has zero external dependencies.
Built-in DI container for all service registrations. Use Scoped for request-bound services, Singleton for app-wide services.
Prefer Minimal APIs for new endpoints. Use controllers for complex scenarios requiring filters or inheritance.
All I/O-bound operations must be async and accept CancellationToken. Never block with .Result or .Wait().
Immutable C# records for all request and response data transfer objects.

guardrail.rule: Never expose domain entities directly in API responses. Always use record DTOs from the Contracts layer and map with Mapster or AutoMapper.
Never make synchronous database calls. All EF Core operations must be awaited with async counterparts (FindAsync, ToListAsync, FirstOrDefaultAsync, SaveChangesAsync).
Never hardcode connection strings or secrets. Use appsettings.json + environment variable overrides. Never commit secrets to source control.
Use a global exception middleware (not per-controller try/catch). All unhandled exceptions must flow through ExceptionMiddleware for consistent error responses and logging.
Include CancellationToken on every async controller action and service method. Pass it through to EF Core and HttpClient calls.
Use [Authorize] on all endpoints that require authentication. Explicitly use [AllowAnonymous] only on public endpoints. Default deny.
Use AsNoTracking() for all read-only EF Core queries. Only track entities that will be modified in the same request.
Use IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> for all EF Core entity configurations. Never configure entities inline in OnModelCreating.
Validate JWT Issuer, Audience, Lifetime, and IssuerSigningKey. Never disable token validation in production.
Target net8.0 (LTS) with Nullable=enable and TreatWarningsAsErrors=true in Directory.Build.props for null-safety across the solution.

project-structure.description: Clean Architecture solution layout: API, Core, Infrastructure, Contracts layers.
project-structure.example: MyApp/ ├── MyApp.Api/ # Web API project (ASP.NET Core host) │ ├── Controllers/ # MVC controllers (complex scenarios) │ ├── Endpoints/ # Minimal API endpoint groups │ ├── Middleware/ # ExceptionMiddleware, etc. │ ├── Validators/ # FluentValidation validators │ ├── Extensions/ # IServiceCollection extension methods │ ├── Program.cs # DI registration and pipeline configuration │ └── appsettings.json # Config (no secrets committed) ├── MyApp.Core/ # Domain layer (ZERO external dependencies) │ ├── Entities/ # Domain entities │ ├── Interfaces/ # Repository and service interfaces │ ├── Services/ # Business logic implementations │ └── Exceptions/ # Domain exception hierarchy ├── MyApp.Infrastructure/ # Data access and external services │ ├── Data/ │ │ ├── AppDbContext.cs │ │ └── Configurations/ # IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> per entity │ └── Repositories/ # Repository implementations ├── MyApp.Contracts/ # Shared DTOs — no project references │ ├── Requests/ # Input records (CreateUserRequest, etc.) │ └── Responses/ # Output records (UserResponse, etc.) ├── tests/ │ ├── MyApp.UnitTests/ # xUnit + Moq + FluentAssertions │ └── MyApp.IntegrationTests/ # WebApplicationFactory + Testcontainers ├── Directory.Build.props # Shared: Nullable, TreatWarningsAsErrors ├── Directory.Packages.props # Central Package Management └── MyApp.sln

notes.note: Core has zero external dependencies — no EF Core, no ASP.NET references
Infrastructure references Core only; Api references Core, Infrastructure, Contracts
Contracts has no project references — shareable with client SDKs

minimal-apis.description: Group endpoints with MapGroup. Use static methods per action. Register in Program.cs.

ef-core.description: DbContext with IEntityTypeConfiguration, audit timestamp intercept, and AsNoTracking for reads.

middleware.description: Global exception middleware maps domain exceptions to HTTP status codes. Register first in pipeline.

di-registration.description: Program.cs registration order: Serilog, DbContext, repositories/services, JWT, health checks, then pipeline.

validation.description: FluentValidation validators registered from assembly. Validate explicitly in Minimal APIs; [ApiController] auto-validates in controllers.

testing.stack: xUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions (unit); WebApplicationFactory + Testcontainers PostgreSQL (integration)

rules.rule: Use Mock<T> from Moq for unit test doubles
Use WebApplicationFactory<Program> + Testcontainers for integration tests
Use IAsyncLifetime for async setup/teardown of containers
Always pass CancellationToken.None in test calls to async service methods

commands.cmd: dotnet ef migrations add MigrationName -p MyApp.Infrastructure -s MyApp.Api
dotnet ef database update -p MyApp.Infrastructure -s MyApp.Api

quick-reference.item: Core (no deps) → Infrastructure → Api → Contracts (no deps); Contracts shared with clients
CancellationToken on every async method; never .Result or .Wait()
C# records in Contracts layer — immutable, serialization-friendly
AsNoTracking() for reads; IEntityTypeConfiguration per entity; SaveChangesAsync with ct
FluentValidation; AbstractValidator per request type; validate in Minimal API handlers explicitly
Global ExceptionMiddleware maps domain exceptions to HTTP codes; never per-controller try/catch
JWT with full token validation; [Authorize] default; [AllowAnonymous] explicit exceptions
xUnit + Moq + FluentAssertions for unit; WebApplicationFactory + Testcontainers for integration
Entity exposure in API, sync DB calls, magic strings (use nameof()), catch-and-swallow exceptions
